writeup.headline: Avantor rates Hold: strong share-price trend and raised guidance offset by a weak balance sheet and slow growth.
writeup.thesis: Avantor scores 52, a Hold, with the factors pulling in different directions. The trend score of 84 is the main support: the price is 49.6% above its 200-day average, 3.5% below its 52-week high, and the shares are 103.5 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. News is also mildly positive, with a Q3 beat and raised FY2026 guidance for organic revenue growth, adjusted EPS and free cash flow. Against that, the balance sheet scores just 9, with net debt at 7.33 times free cash flow and cash covering only 0.13 of debt. Growth (43) is modest, with TTM revenue growth of 0.9%, although latest-quarter revenue growth of 4.6% year on year shows growth sped up by 4.1 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation (45) is middling: in absolute terms P/FCF of 25.8x and EV/EBIT of 29.8x are not low, the FCF yield is 1.1 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and overall the multiples sit near the middle of their own history, though P/FCF is more expensive than at 56 of the last 61 month-ends.
key_risks: High leverage: net debt at 7.33 times free cash flow and a low cash-to-debt ratio of 0.13.
Thin margins: an operating margin of 7.3% and an FCF margin of 6.6%, with VWR's margin falling and pricing lagging inflation.
After a sharp run-up, the price is 49.6% above its 200-day average, so the strong trend score could fade quickly.
The 2025 securities class action is still pending.
Analysts remain cautious, with ratings at Hold or Underweight despite raised price targets.
what_would_change: A move up to Buy needs 13 more points, for example sustained revenue acceleration lifting the growth score along with debt reduction improving the balance sheet score.
A drop below 45 (8 points away) to Sell could come if the share-price trend reverses and the trend score falls from 84.
A guidance cut or a renewed revenue slowdown would weigh on both the news and growth scores.
Stronger free cash flow would help both the balance sheet and valuation scores, by lowering net debt to FCF and improving the FCF yield.
